english.title: Use semen, embryos or ova collected from pigs during 30 days prior to vaccination against classical swine fever (Wales)
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), where classical swine fever had been confirmed and the appropriate authority was concerned that it threatened to spread to other areas, used

(A)_[semen]_
(B)_[embryos]_
(C)_[ova]_

collected from pigs during the 30 days prior to vaccination, during the vaccination period within an emergency vaccination zone other than under a licence granted by a veterinary inspector
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 29(13)(c) and 39(1)(j) and (2) of the Diseases of Swine Regulations 2014.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: From 29th April 2026, due to changes made by the Exotic Animal Disease (Amendment) (England) Order 2026 (SI 2026/475), this offence applies in Wales. For the offence applying before this date, see H19867 and for the offence applying in England, see H102729.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time Limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
